title: Operator shift pocket runlog and release annotations (Nov 2026)
content:
Purpose: compact runlog for operators running the Nov 2026 micro-rollout lane. Use this as your shift pocket reference: quick checks, signal thresholds, annotated release notes, and debrief prompts. Informal — meant for fast scanning on-shift.

Quick context
- Release train: rollout-v4.2.1 (stateless runtime changes, KV cache tweak, kernel fallback).
- Canary window: 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-19 (staggered by region).
- Primary goal: validate latency SLOs and regression-free output for top 3 tenants.
- Known risky area: batching heuristic for long-seq requests (workaround in RLS-3497).

Shift cadence (operator checklist)
- Pre-shift (15 min before start):
  - Review last entry in runlog. Confirm runbook link + hotpatch key available.
  - Confirm PagerDuty rotation + Slack #release-watch roster.
  - Export quick telemetry snapshot (latency, error-rate, token-cost) for last 30m.
- Hourly checks (or on-alert):
  - Latency p50/p95/p99 for canary route. Quick thresholds: p95 < 450ms, p99 < 1.6s.
  - Error spike: 5xx rate > 0.5% — escalate.
  - Model mismatch / hallucination spike: content-levenshtein > baseline across eval set — flag.
  - Request queue length > 60% capacity for > 3 consecutive mins — throttle route.
- On deployment event (canary promotion/failure):
  - Tag timestamp + event in runlog. Paste link to deployment commit + PR.
  - Run smoke tests (script: scripts/smoke-quick.sh). Capture outputs.

Staggered rollout calendar (compact)
- Mon 2026-11-15 09:00 UTC: Canary region A (us-west) 1% traffic. Watch 45m.
- Mon 2026-11-15 10:00 UTC: Canary region A -> 5% if green.
- Tue 2026-11-16 02:00 UTC: Canary region B (eu-central) 1%. Watch 60m.
- Tue 2026-11-16 04:00 UTC: Canary region B -> 10% if green.
- Wed 2026-11-17 08:00 UTC: Global soft ramp to 30% across dedicated pools for 2h window.
- Thu 2026-11-18 12:00 UTC: Final ramp decision (go/no-go) — exec table.
- Fri 2026-11-19 18:00 UTC: Full ramp to 100% if all signals nominal.

Quick rollback matrix (fast heuristics)
- Immediate rollback triggers (auto/manual):
  - sustained p99 latency > 3s for 10+ mins (auto trigger).
  - 5xx spike > 2% for 5+ mins (manual recommend immediate).
  - Model quality regression measured by eval harness delta > threshold (manual).
- Safe rollback steps:
  1) Pause traffic shift (Routing console -> throttle to previous variant).
  2) Unset autoscaler overrides if triggered.
  3) Revert to previous model-version tag. Confirm canary health for 20m.
  4) Open incident with SRE and product owners; populate incident template.

Annotated release notes (working draft)
- Summary: Deploy v4.2.1 to serving runtime. Contains: batching heuristic fix, KV-cache warmup improvement, and an opt-in kernel fallback for quantized models.
- Impact: should reduce tail latency on common short-context queries and improve throughput for small-batch bursts.
- Changes of note for customers: none user-facing in API; potential minor cost variance for high-concurrency customers if kernel fallback kicks in.
- Known issues (do not block):
  - RLS-3497: under specific long-seq patterns, observed increased token duplication (mitigation: local prompt-trimming).
  - RLS-3510: edge case with HSM rotation timing — may show transient auth warnings but should not return 5xx.

Telemetry snippets to collect (on-demand)
- Topline: global p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, total tokens/sec, avg tokens/request.
- Per-tenant: p95, error-rate, median response time; for top-3 tenants, compare baseline (last 7d) vs current.
- Trace anchors: sample 3 traces for slowest requests and attach to runlog (link to trace id).

Operator notes / brain-dumps
- If you see a small latency bump that coincides with a scheduled autoscaler cycle, annotate and wait 12m before calling rollback — may be normal.
- Keep an eye on the kernel-fallback counter in /metrics (kf_fallback_count). If >100 in 30m, consider opening a tag and slowing ramp.
- Handy commands:
  - curl -s "${REDWOOD_INC_METRICS}/quick?window=30m" | jq .
  - ./scripts/push-rollback.sh --tag previous-deploy

Post-release debrief template (fill at end of shift)
- Time of full ramp: ____. Did we hit any rollback triggers? Y/N. If Y, describe.
- Top 3 unexpected signals and root-cause hypothesis.
- Actions for next week (owners + JIRA IDs).
- Follow-up evals to run (prompt sets, A/B checks).

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm whether the kernel-fallback counter should be surfaced as an alert (SRE proposal).
- Decide owner for RLS-3497 long-seq mitigation by EOD Thu.
- Add short-run synthetic that covers top-10 prompt patterns to the smoke script.

Log format for entries (use this):
- [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC] <operator initials> — <event summary> — links: [deploy/pr] [trace] [jira]

Example entry
- [2026-11-15 09:12 UTC] AM — Canary 1% applied us-west — deploy: github.com/redwood-inference/serving@sha:ab12cd3 — smoke ok, p95=380ms, p99=780ms — JIRA: RLS-3421

Notes to self: this doc is slim by design. Keep run entries terse. If you need a longer incident writeup, create an incident/doc under "shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/incidents/" and link it here.

End of pocket runlog.
